This article examines the exclusion criteria and unreported data points for patients evaluated in the Danish [[atrieflimren]] registry, specifically focusing on the calculations for [[indikator-1|Indikator 1]] and [[indikator-8|Indikator 8]]. Understanding these exclusions is critical for assessing the true denominator of patients eligible for quality-of-care metrics, particularly regarding [[antikoagulationsbehandling]].

For [[indikator-1|Indikator 1]], the leading reason for exclusion in both the 2023 and 2024 reports is the lack of clinical indication for [[antikoagulationsbehandling]], defined as a [[cha2ds2-vasc|CHA2DS2-VASc]] score of less than 2. In 2023, this accounted for 8,262 exclusions [^src1]. By 2024, this number had increased to 9,158, remaining the overwhelmingly dominant exclusion category [^src3]. The trailing exclusion reason in 2023 was patients lacking Danish residence or holding a substitute CPR number, with 269 cases [^src1]. In 2024, this group slightly increased to 274, but the absolute lowest exclusion count was a new category for patients with an unknown municipality of residence, which accounted for only 9 individuals [^src3]. 

Comparing the two reporting periods for [[indikator-1|Indikator 1]], several trends and outliers emerge. The number of patients excluded due to death within 30 days of diagnosis decreased from 471 in 2023 to 430 in 2024 [^src1] [^src3]. Furthermore, the 2024 data introduces two new exclusion categories not present in the 2023 table: 773 patients were excluded because they were not incident cases (having another AF diagnosis within the last 10 years), and 9 patients were excluded due to an unknown municipality [^src3]. 

For [[indikator-8|Indikator 8]], the 2023 data shows a different exclusion profile. The leading reason for exclusion was patient death within one year of the diagnosis date, accounting for 2,242 individuals [^src2]. The trailing reason was the lack of Danish residence or possession of a substitute CPR number, with 237 exclusions [^src2]. 

For comprehensive data on other indicators, regional variations, and longitudinal trends not captured in these specific exclusion tables, readers should consult the full annual reports for 2023 and 2024 [^src4] [^src5] [^src6] [^src7] [^src8] [^src9] [^src10] [^src11] [^src12] [^src13] [^src14] [^src15] [^src16] [^src17] [^src18] [^src19] [^src20] [^src21] [^src22].
